title: All-providers-failed data errors reach panels as raw Python exception strings, with no 'what would unlock it'
repro: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:52152/quotes/ZZZQNOPE -> 502 {"detail":"yfinance quote failed for 'ZZZQNOPE': 'PriceHistory' object has no attribute '_dividends'"}; the Equity Overview / Watchlist / Chart panels print that string verbatim
notes: spec Edge-Cases-Pass-B promises an honest 'unavailable' + reason + what would unlock it. D43's humanizer (services/errors.py) covers LLM errors only; ProviderError has a `kind` taxonomy but the global handler ignores it. Smallest fix: map ProviderError.kind -> {message, action} in the app.py handler (reuse errors.HumanError shape) and have panels render message+action with raw detail behind the existing toggle.

title: Portfolio market value / P&L carry no freshness badge — stale or after-hours quotes read as live
repro: design: open Portfolio after IN close (or with a Yahoo-throttled stale quote); value + P&L render with no live/EOD/stale label while Watchlist shows one for the same quote
evidence: src/modules/portfolio/PortfolioPanel.tsx:140-166 (quotes fetched, only fetch failure badged), src/modules/watchlist/WatchlistPanel.tsx:75 (badge exists elsewhere), sidecar/services/locale.py:225-254
notes: spec Edge-Cases + FR-041: stale/after-hours data never shown as live. The Quote already carries `freshness`; smallest fix = reuse StalenessBadge per row + a summary-level 'as of' on the totals.

title: Native web search has no per-RUN cap off-Anthropic and per-search billing is never metered
repro: design: tier_a + a native-search model on OpenAI/Gemini/xAI/OpenRouter -> opts['web_search_max_uses'] is popped by the adapter; the loop counter only counts the local `web_search` tool, which is withheld on the native tier
evidence: sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1335-1340,1416,1553-1561; sidecar/services/llm/openai.py:664-667; sidecar/services/llm/gemini.py:110-112; sidecar/services/llm/native_search.py:109-113 (comment promises a loop-level counter that is not there); sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:82-84; src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:921
notes: spec Edge-Cases (FR-081): per-run search cap + legible cost-so-far. Anthropic cap is per request (x6 rounds). BudgetGuard prices tokens only, so a $10/1k-search lane is invisible to the spend ceiling and the UI. Smallest fix: count native searches from adapter usage/citation metadata per round, stop sending web_search=True once the run total hits the cap, add a per-search rate to model_registry prices and surface it in cost().

title: yfinance is still the de-facto India primary for fundamentals/statements/analyst
repro: design: provider_registry candidates for model_key='fundamentals', region IN = openbb-mcp (all-null shells for IN, D72) -> yfinance; no exchange-direct / filing-derived fundamentals provider exists
notes: spec Edge-Cases-Pass-B: 'yfinance is never the trusted India primary'. Holds for quote/OHLC only. D73 proved yfinance is 'present-but-subtly-off' below mid-cap (141x institutional holding, promoter drift). Cross-checks flag some fields but the primary number shown is still yfinance's. Likely overlaps the data-battery sweeps — merge there. Fix shape: an exchange/XBRL-derived IN fundamentals provider ranked above yfinance for the fields it can serve.

title: Agent surface has no full-cockpit mode — width hard-capped at 1200px
repro: Drag the agent-dock resize handle to the right on any viewport >= ~1600px wide -> the column stops growing at 1200px; there is no toggle/command that lets it occupy the full cockpit.
evidence: src/components/AgentDock.tsx:19-133, src/store/agent-dock.ts:12-13 (AGENT_DOCK_MIN_WIDTH=280, AGENT_DOCK_MAX_WIDTH=1200 hard px cap)
notes: spec.md FR-001 MUST: the agent surface can occupy 'a dominant column OR the full cockpit'. Only the dominant-column half is built; the full-cockpit mode (agent as the sole/maximized surface) doesn't exist in any form. Smallest fix: a maximize toggle that sets width to the viewport width (or a CSS flex-basis: 100% state) alongside the existing collapse.

title: Four explicit hotkey-switchable agent intents (Ask/Edit-panel/Build/Delegate) collapsed to two, with no formal decision record
repro: Open the app; try alt+3 / alt+4 (the old Build/Edit-panel bindings) -> nothing happens; only alt+1 (inferred 'Agent') and alt+2 (Delegate) exist.
evidence: types/agent-modes.ts:1-60 (own docblock: 'The old four explicit modes ... collapses the three hands-on modes into ONE inferred surface'), src/store/keybindings.ts:65-76 (comment: 'the shipped handler no longer has' the alt+1-4 bindings), docs/redesign/R4_STALE_CODE_REGISTER.md:62 (S-15 flags the FR-003-vs-Track-B conflict as an unresolved 'two mode systems coexist' item)
notes: spec.md FR-003 is an explicit MUST for four named modes on stable global hotkeys with the active mode always visible. The shipped two-mode inferred surface may be a reasonable product call, but no D-number in docs/redesign/DECISIONS.md or CHANGELOG.md entry formally records the reversal the way COMMON.md's decision_ref format requires — R4_STALE_CODE_REGISTER.md flagged the conflict as something to 'decide' and it was resolved in code without a paper trail. Smallest fix: either restore the four-mode dispatch, or add a one-line DECISIONS.md/CHANGELOG.md entry ratifying the two-mode collapse so this doesn't keep resurfacing as a spec/code mismatch.

title: Delegate runs can never self-pause to ask a question — only an external/operator-driven pause exists
repro: Start a Delegate run and let it hit a point where it would benefit from asking the user something mid-run -> it has no ask_user-style tool; it either keeps guessing or runs to completion/budget-breach, it cannot pause itself.
evidence: sidecar/services/run_manager.py:23-33 ('the pause is an EXPLICIT signal (operator/host-driven), not an autonomous in-loop ask_user tool call ... which is deferred')
notes: spec.md FR-028 (SHOULD): 'pause for a human-in-the-loop question without losing progress.' The pause/answer/resume plumbing is fully built and durable; only the agent's own ability to trigger a pause is missing, and it's self-documented in code as deferred (no ask_user catalog capability yet). Smallest fix: add an ask_user Capability (read-only, internal-only) that calls pause_run().

title: BYOK/credential setup is split across two separate UIs, neither offers a test-connection action
repro: Open Settings > AI Providers to add an LLM key (one form) vs Settings > Integrations -> 'Open Marketplace' to add a broker/data-connector credential (a different panel, different form) -> no single place to manage every connector's credentials; after saving either, there is no 'Test connection' button, only a passive background readiness probe for LLM keys.
evidence: src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:410-530 (ProvidersSection, LLM-only) and :1563-1585 (IntegrationsSection just links out: 'Broker connections are managed in the Marketplace'), src/modules/marketplace/MarketplacePanel.tsx:35,118,244 (separate credentialFields form), grep for a user-triggered test action across SettingsPanel.tsx/MarketplacePanel.tsx/KeyEntryDialog.tsx is empty
notes: spec.md FR-034 MUST: 'a single BYOK/credentials hub' that renders/masks/tests forms generically for every data provider, broker, and connector. Shipped has two separate, differently-implemented surfaces and no explicit test affordance on either. Smallest fix: fold IntegrationsSection's credential rendering into the same generic component ProvidersSection uses (or vice versa), and add a Test button that fires one cheap read call through the credential.

title: Settings export/import drops every configured connection — only keybindings + 3 preference fields travel
repro: Configure an LLM provider default, a broker plugin, and a data-connector, then Settings > Export settings -> open the downloaded vysted-settings.json -> it contains only keybindingOverrides + {defaultAgentId, region, deepResearchBackend}; none of the above survive an export/import round-trip (secrets aside).
evidence: src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:1757-1791 (SettingsExport shape), src/store/settings.ts:51-68 (SettingsBundle = {defaultAgentId, region, deepResearchBackend} only; useLLMProvidersStore.defaultProviderId is not part of it)
notes: spec.md FR-037 (SHOULD): 'Configured connections SHOULD be exportable/importable across machines (secrets via the keychain, not the export file).' Today the non-secret SHAPE of a connection (which providers/brokers/connectors are set up, default provider) isn't exported at all, so a machine move means reconfiguring everything from scratch even though no secret needed to travel. Smallest fix: add a connections field to SettingsExport (provider ids, default provider, installed marketplace plugin ids + their non-secret config) alongside the existing keybindings/settings.

title: Settings surface is missing most of the FR-038 preference categories — no provider/model order, palette behavior, panel defaults, or starter-cockpit composition controls
repro: Open Settings and look for a way to set a provider/model FALLBACK ORDER (only a single 'Default' radio-style pick exists, src/store/llm-providers.ts:127-136), or to configure command-palette ranking behavior, or to change which panels open in the default per-launch cockpit -> none exist.
evidence: src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx section list (ProvidersSection:410, ResearchSection:1210, RegionSection:1297, KeybindingsSection:1365, AdvancedSection:1532, IntegrationsSection:1563, LayoutsSection:1587, ModulesSection:1710, ExportImportSection:1775, AboutSection:1872) and src/store/settings.ts:51-68 (SettingsBundle covers only defaultAgentId/region/deepResearchBackend)
notes: spec.md FR-038 MUST, 'depth target is Cursor-grade': keybindings (delivered), default persona (delivered), default provider/model + PREFERENCE ORDER (only a single default pick, no order list), palette behavior (absent), panel defaults (absent), starter-cockpit composition (absent — src/config/default-layout.ts is a hardcoded constant with no settings-surface editor), theming knobs (N/A, dark-only by FR-030). Several explicitly-named categories in an explicit MUST have zero UI. Smallest fix (biggest win first): a provider preference-order list (drag-to-reorder over the existing provider rows) and a starter-cockpit panel picker feeding src/config/default-layout.ts.

title: Panels are not marketplace-installable — a second, parallel 'module' extension system exists alongside the plugin contract
repro: Open the Marketplace panel and look for any of the core panels (Chart, Watchlist, Portfolio, News, ...) as an installable/removable entry -> none are listed; they ship as hardcoded 'modules' instead.
evidence: src/lib/module-registry.ts:1-14 ('A first-party module bundles panels, commands... Modules are the in-app analogue of the VystedPlugin panel/command capabilities'), plugins/ contains broker + data-provider + one agent-pack plugin but no panel-contributing plugin (grep for `panels:` across plugins/*/index.ts finds none)
notes: spec.md FR-050 MUST: 'brokers, data providers/connectors, panels, and agents are all delivered as marketplace plugins ... one unified extension model.' Brokers/data/agents genuinely go through the marketplace; panels are still a separate, build-time-registered VystedModule system the user cannot install, configure, or remove at runtime — the module-registry's own docblock names itself an 'analogue' of the plugin contract, i.e. a second parallel system, not the same one. Smallest fix (large): give PanelSpec-contributing modules a manifest + marketplace entry point, or explicitly re-scope FR-050 to exclude first-party panels with a recorded decision.

title: Data-provider credential/shape declaration lives in a hand-maintained duplicate, disconnected from both the plugin contract and the provider registry
repro: Trace where a marketplace entry's credentialFields (e.g. an API-key form) comes from -> it's a literal array hand-written in src/lib/marketplace.ts, not derived from sidecar/services/provider_registry.py's ProviderDeclaration (which has no credentials field at all) nor from types/plugin.ts's VystedPlugin contract (which also has no credentialFields).
evidence: types/marketplace.ts:59 (CredentialField/credentialFields declared here, NOT in types/plugin.ts — grep for credentialFields in types/plugin.ts is empty), src/lib/marketplace.ts:150,202,219,245,262,279,296,322 (credentialFields arrays hand-written per entry, several via a keySecretFields() helper), sidecar/services/provider_registry.py:80-99 (ProviderDeclaration = {id, serves, rank, requires, asset_classes, region} — no credentials/shape field)
notes: spec.md FR-053 MUST: the data registry's credential+shape declaration IS the data-source slice of the one unified plugin/marketplace model — not a second, separately-maintained description. In code there are three disconnected surfaces: the Tier-1 VystedPlugin contract (no credential concept), the provider registry (no credential concept), and a hand-maintained types/marketplace.ts + src/lib/marketplace.ts literal list that the project's own single-source-of-truth catalog convention (CLAUDE.md's capability-catalog rule) would normally forbid. Smallest fix: add a credentials field to ProviderDeclaration and derive src/lib/marketplace.ts's entries from it (or from plugin manifests) instead of hand-writing them.
